facts.statement: Gavialinum is an extinct genus of teleosaurid thalattosuchian crocodilomorph.
facts.quote: Gavialinum es un género extinto de crocodilomorfo talatosuquio teleosáurido.

facts.statement: Gavialinum rhodani had a long, narrow snout similar to modern gavialids, which inspired the genus name.
facts.quote: Gavialinum rhodani has a long, narrow snout, much like the current gavialids, from which the Gavialinum genus gets its name.

facts.statement: Gavialinum possessed 33 teeth in each jaw, totaling 66 teeth.
facts.quote: Gavialinum had 33 teeth on each jaw, for a total of 66.

facts.statement: Gavialinum rhodoni had a long and narrow snout very similar to that of modern gavialids, from which the genus Gavialinum takes its name.
facts.quote: Gavialinum rhodoni tenía un hocico largo y estrecho, muy similar al de los actuales gaviálidos, de los que el género Gavialinum toma su nombre.

facts.statement: Despite the snout resemblance, Gavialinum rhodani was not closely related to modern crocodilians because it appeared before true crocodilians evolved.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, esto no significa que estén relacionados de cerca, ya que Gavialinum rhodoni apareció antes que los crocodilianos verdaderos.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gavialinum have been found in France dating to the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in France that date back to the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Its fossils have been found in France in rocks dating from the Bathonian epoch of the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han encontrado en Francia en rocas que datan de la época del Bathoniense del Jurásico Medio.

facts.statement: The genus Gavialinum was described by Lortet in 1892.
The genus authority for Gavialinum is Lortet, 1892.
The Paleobiology Database lists the genus name as Gavialinum, attributed to Jourdan in 1892.
Gavialinum lived during the Bathonian stage, between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gavialinum is classified within the unranked order Mesoeucrocodylia.
Gavialinum belongs to the suborder Thalattosuchia.
Gavialinum is a member of the family Teleosauridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Gavialidae as the parent group for Gavialinum.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Gavialinum within the family Gavialidae.
